newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen heading higher, eyes 2,750 points.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen heading higher, eyes 2,750 points.

text.p: Germany's DAX index was expected to continue a steady climb this week and could reach 2,750 points, after jumping to new record levels on Tuesday on Wall Street strength and gains in the dollar and German debt.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares, hit a new high of 2,734.37 after the Dow Jones forged ahead in early trade.
The IBIS later slipped back somewhat on profit-taking to trade at 2,720.19, up 19.36 points. The DAX closed floor dealings up 34.55 points at a new closing record of 2,727.28.
"We can go on further from these levels," said one trader.

Dealers said Western European car registration figures out after the end of trade on Monday had given a boost to auto stocks, which, as major exporters, were also boosted by the strength of the dollar.
Car manufacturer Daimler Benz AG was the DAX's biggest climber, adding over three percent after the news to trade up 2.16 in IBIS dealings to stand at 86.62 marks.

Tehcnical analysts also said the automobile sector was supported by technical factors. "There are buy signals in Daimler AG and BMW AG, while utilities and chemicals are also looking very good technically," said one.
